costScope: Full ordinary unrestricted recipient gift, analytically normalized to C=$100,000. All portfolio/support costs remain in the denominator. E/Y is total recipient expense per nominal annual SSP person, NOT SSP-only unit cost. No naloxone purchase price, restricted gift allocation or extra leverage is assumed. Third-party incremental resource costs remain unknown; this is a donor-dollar rather than societal-cost estimate.
geographicAttribution: g_CA=0.98 central, 1 favorable and 0.9 adverse are explicit judgments about where direct survivor health is enjoyed. Sacramento and neighboring California service geography is observed; longitudinal residency/migration is not. No population-share or headquarters allocation.
formula: C/E*Y*d*m*x*network gives an expected additional unique risk-person cohort, capped at judgment K: N=min(...,K). From donation time until delay L both arms have hazard h=lambda+mu. During min(tau,T-L) the intervention reduces only opioid fatal hazard by lambda*e; afterward both arms have postLambda+postMu. Integrate u*(S_with-S_without)*exp(-r*t) over [0,T], then subtract harmPerProtected per N and independentHarm per gift. Q_CA=g*Q_all; scenario cost=C+extraResources; price_10_CA=10*(C+extraResources)/Q_CA only if Q_CA>0. Closed form: H=max(0,T-L),b=min(tau,H),A(k,z)=-expm1(-k*z)/k; q=u*exp(-(h+r)*L)*[A(h-lambda*e+r,b)-A(h+r,b)+exp(-h*b)*expm1(lambda*e*b)*exp(-r*b)*A(postLambda+postMu+r,H-b)]. Q_all=N*(q-harmPerProtected)-independentHarm. Delayed protection is discounted and survives baseline risk before delivery; no repeated-lifetime awards.
counterfactual: Existing HRS portfolio, grants, state-supplied naloxone, other distributors, informal sharing and EMS continue without the donation. The central m=0.5 allows half proportional service expansion to disappear through replacement, reserves or capacity constraints. The e=0.1 reduction is incremental versus available alternative responses, not the biological reversal success rate.
attribution: Count the expected unique-person cohort once, not a new lifetime for every kit or reported reversal. Use the full recipient cost so no extra program-allocation factor is applied. Give no additional QALY credit here to HIV/HCV prevention, case management, clinic care or treatment navigation because joint marginal pathways are unresolved; this is a partial-health portfolio estimate, not a demonstrated lower bound. Shared delivery and existing public naloxone are incorporated through marginal delivery/effect assumptions, without claiming that donor cash purchases the drug. The network factor translates eligible recipients/rescuers into distinct protected people at opioid risk, without multiplying kit or rescue counts. K caps incremental risk-person capacity, not gross service reach. These new quantities remain unmeasured judgments.
uncertainty: Subjective conditional central scenario, not an identified HRS treatment effect, statistical expected value or confidence interval. Original full-recipient accounts anchor cost; current unique risk-people, marginal capacity, alternative response and clinical transfer remain judgments. Twenty-three joint and single-parameter stresses include zero and hypothetical negative health. Other portfolio benefits are unquantified, and central unmeasured harms are set to zero only within this partial model; stress scenarios do not establish their empirical size. This is not a demonstrated lower bound or donor endorsement.
nativeOutcomes: Central 36.85208868794182 expected protected risk-people, 0.3303339760121013 all-population QALYs, 0.3237272964918593 California QALYs per $100,000. The central estimate is preserved, not newly observed. The $100,000 gift implies $2713.55 per modeled additional protected risk-person, not per kit, reversal or permanently prevented death. At one year, the model has 0.07017973857388961 extra survivors across all geographies; later mortality continues to erode that difference. No observed cost per usable dose or extra rescue can be calculated from the available inventory and delivery data.

inputs.name: C
inputs.rationale: Analytical normalization only; not an observed expansion request.

inputs.name: E
inputs.rationale: FY ending June 2025 original Form 990 Part IX total; all programs and support retained.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.rationale: Schedule O reports approximately this scale; the wording and number are repeated in FY2023, so freshness and deduplication are not established. It is not verified additional or unique reach.

inputs.name: d
inputs.unit: current unique share of nominal reach
inputs.rationale: Halve repeated self-reported annual scale because no fresh deduplicated series is available; scenario range 0.2–1, not an empirical interval.

inputs.name: m
inputs.unit: marginal delivery relative to proportional average scale
inputs.rationale: Allow half otherwise proportional expansion to replace funding, replenish reserves or fail to add capacity. SSP reliance on donations makes positive delivery plausible; reserves/grants prevent assuming 100%. Range 0.1–0.8, with separate zero case.

inputs.name: x
inputs.unit: share with relevant sustained opioid-overdose protection
inputs.rationale: Not every SSP recipient uses opioids or gains a usable response network. Current SSP distributes Narcan and includes mobile outreach; reported training covers only 500 annually, so no assumption that all SSP recipients are newly trained. Range 0.2–0.8. This selects usable access among eligible opioid-risk recipients; e separately represents their conditional mortality reduction and does not repeat reach or funding discounts.

inputs.name: lambda
inputs.rationale: External risk calibration, not HRS observation. Older California post-overdose ED cohort had 1,863 unintentional overdose deaths/100,000 person-years; Ontario cohort had 1.9% opioid-related mortality in one year. Both are selected recent-overdose cohorts, not general SSP users, and predate the current fentanyl environment. Range 0.005–0.04 is subjective.

inputs.name: mu
inputs.rationale: Combined central all-cause hazard is 0.05/year; Ontario post-overdose all-cause mortality was 5.3%. Constant long-run hazard is a simplifying prior, not cohort survival follow-up. Range 0.02–0.05. The added beta stress also considers 0.10/year; stated earlier range is not the complete set of sensitivities.

inputs.name: e
inputs.unit: incremental proportional opioid-fatal hazard reduction while protected
inputs.rationale: Discounted transfer judgment: older ecological OEND study associated implementation with 27–46% lower community mortality, whereas recent bundled cluster trial estimated RR 0.91 with CI 0.76–1.09. Neither identifies individual HRS effect. Central 10%, stress 1–25%, plus zero, explicitly accounts for other responders and existing naloxone.

inputs.name: tau
inputs.rationale: One finite year, not permanent risk removal or one year for every repeated kit. Adverse 0.25 year.

inputs.name: T
inputs.rationale: Finite horizon; adverse 5, favorable 20. Continued high mortality in both arms prevents fresh full lifetimes after recurrent rescues.

inputs.name: u
inputs.rationale: Health-state utility assumption, not a value assigned to the person. Stress 0.5–0.8; no HRS utility measurement.

inputs.name: r
inputs.rationale: Explicit modeling convention in all scenarios.

inputs.name: g_CA
inputs.rationale: Mostly local direct beneficiaries, with allowance for migration; stress 0.9–1.

inputs.name: incremental third-party cost
inputs.rationale: Public drug stock, partner clinician time and other induced costs are not measured; societal cost-effectiveness would require them.

inputs.name: network
inputs.unit: distinct protected risk-people per otherwise eligible response-network equivalent
inputs.rationale: Central 1 is an unmeasured translation, not one kit or attendee equals one beneficiary. Half-translation stress; de-duplicate across responders.

inputs.name: K
inputs.rationale: Judgment nonbinding cap of 100; five-person stress. Not verified deliverable capacity or room-for-funding. Favorable 1000 is likewise hypothetical.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.rationale: Zero central for maintenance/immediate delivery is a judgment; six-month delivery stress, survival/discount applied. NDP administrative timelines are not HRS delivery evidence.

inputs.name: postLambda
inputs.unit: annual opioid fatality hazard after protection
inputs.rationale: Central same as baseline; higher recurrent-risk stress avoids assuming indefinite rescue survival.

inputs.name: postMu
inputs.unit: annual other-cause mortality hazard after protection
inputs.rationale: Central same as baseline; high competing mortality stress.

inputs.name: harmPerProtected
inputs.unit: discounted QALYs lost per protected risk-person
inputs.rationale: Central zero unmeasured burden within partial model, not evidence of no harm; .01 subjective burden stress.

inputs.name: independentHarm
inputs.unit: discounted all-population QALYs lost per gift
inputs.rationale: Central zero; .05 hypothetical gift-level harm can occur even with zero delivery. Not an HRS observed harm estimate.

inputs.name: extraResources
inputs.unit: incremental unpriced partner/public USD per gift
inputs.rationale: Central zero add-on for donor-dollar display, NOT assertion societal resources cost zero. Hypothetical $100,000 supplement tests total-resource price separately.

sensitivity: Central price is about $3.1 million per ten California QALYs; favorable about $75,000 and adverse about $38 billion. These simultaneous stress scenarios are not statistical confidence bounds.

Using only the reported 500 annual overdose-training participants as Y, without changing any other factor, divides benefit by ten and raises price to $30.89 million. This is a consequential alternative, not proof that existing SSP participants lack protective naloxone.
Replacing latest E with verified three-year expense mean $1,899,047.67 raises central price to $3,458,905.01. No cash-only expense series is inferred by subtracting donated contributions.
At fixed risk/survival assumptions, halving d, m, x or g halves QALYs and doubles price. d and m represent different mechanisms: reported unique/current scale versus financing additionality.
At central per-person q=0.00896377893 and g=0.98, $1 million per ten QALYs requires approximately 113.84 additionally protected people per $100,000; $100,000 requires 1,138.37. Central yields 36.85.
Zero is not excluded, and the favorable number is not an achievable offer. If the gift only sustains existing services that would otherwise continue, the incremental branch vanishes.

Beta: nonbinding central capacity K=100 is hypothetical; $1m/ten-QALY target needs 113.84 protected people at central survival, above this cap. It requires revising the capacity assumption, not merely spending more linearly.
Higher post-protection mortality reduces central benefit; drug treatment and protection must not be inferred to persist for the ten-year survival-accounting window.
Hypothetical harms can exceed the central 0.00896 QALY survival gain per protected risk-person. These tests are not empirical estimates of HRS harm.
missingInputs: Fresh privacy-preserving annual unique SSP reach and overlap with training, opioid use and actual response networks.
Marginal staffing/outreach plan and unrestricted cash requirement; current grants, replacement behavior, restricted balances and capacity.
California client baseline fatality risk and differential timely response with versus without HRS, not reported reversal counts.
Duration of useful protection, recurrent mortality, utility and migration follow-up.
Joint non-overlapping HIV/HCV, treatment and clinic effects; incremental public/partner resource costs.
Whether the paused library route was replaced elsewhere; current access constraints and a feasible protected-person expansion cap.
Current opioid-settlement and other public/private grant values, allowed SSP versus other costs, current NDP/clearinghouse inventory and restrictions.
Independent CPA statements and donated clinical partner resource quantities needed for full societal cost; 990 audit checkboxes and blank Schedule D reconciliations do not fill this gap.
